$comment: The only RETRIABLE block: a velocity window clears on its own, so an SDK may back off and try again. Every other block needs a person to change something. This rule is also decided a second time by the database, atomically, because an in-memory window would be correct for one signer process and silently wrong the day there are two — if the two ever disagree, the database is right.

cases.name: pass · prior spend well inside the window limit
boundary · a sum EXACTLY equal to the limit is allowed
boundary · one micro-USDC over the limit is refused
boundary · an entry EXACTLY 600 seconds old is OUTSIDE the window
cases.$why: now is 14:00:00 and the window is 600s, so 13:50:00 is the cutoff. An entry at exactly the cutoff has aged out. This boundary is asserted twice: here, and against the real database aggregation.

cases.name: boundary · an entry one second inside the window still counts
